messages.subject: fixed truncation out-of-range behavior
parts:
I fixed the truncation out-of-range behavior.
For a dummy model with truncation

model {
y ~ normal(0,1) T[-2,2];
y ~ normal(0,10) T[-3,];
y ~ normal(0,10) T[,4];
y ~ normal(-1,5);
}

Here's what gets generated now:

lp__ += stan::prob::normal_log<true>(y, 0, 1);

if (y < -(2)) lp__ -= std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
else if (y > 2) lp__ -= std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
else lp__ -= log(normal_cdf(2, 0, 1) - normal_cdf(-(2), 0, 1));

lp__ += stan::prob::normal_log<true>(y, 0, 10);
if (y < -(3)) lp__ -= std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
else lp__ -= log1m(normal_cdf(-(3), 0, 10));

lp__ += stan::prob::normal_log<true>(y, 0, 10);
if (y > 4) lp__ -= std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
else lp__ -= log(normal_cdf(4, 0, 10));

lp__ += stan::prob::normal_log<true>(y, -(1), 5);

It could still be a bit more efficient in the error condition
by not evaluating normal_log at all. In fact, if the
bounds happen, I could just return -infinity from the
function.

I'm a little uncertain what to do here. I'd have thrown
a domain_error, but we decided to return -inf in these cases
instead.

- Bob
